summary: Today’s pulse tracks Investigators begin work on why cargo plane overran Miami runway, Policing minister makes statement on ‘intimidating and thuggish’ anti-migrant protests – UK politics live, and Alleged killers of Australian surfers and American friend go on trial in Mexico. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are nuclear, american, and australian. In the background, Polanski faces Green rival in his pursuit of Keir Starmer’s old seat and Syrian reactor could have been used for nuclear weapons if completed, UN says keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Investigators begin work on why cargo plane overran Miami runway
headlines.description: Five people died and five others were injured as the Amazon plane overshot the runway after landing at Miami International Airport.

headlines.title: Policing minister makes statement on ‘intimidating and thuggish’ anti-migrant protests – UK politics live
headlines.description: Sarah Jones tells MPs ‘those responsible should expect to face the consequences’ Healey says Andy Burnham set out in his statement to MPs last week what he thought had gone wrong The fundamentals of our economy [were] hollowed out through a series of past policy decisions, political power was centralised, weakening the relationships between the people, the businesses and the institutions who can make things happen beyond Whitehall. The economic enablers were privatised and outsourced, leaving accountability to a thicket of arm’s length bodies and regulators, too often without the predictability or the pace that underpins a thriving market economy. And our country was deindustrialised as the cost to make anything, to build anything here soared, and our dependence on unreliable sources grew, including in areas critical to our national security and sovereignty. Let me be clear, I recognise that the costs of business, its energy bills, regulation, burdens, planning constraints, labour costs, have grown since Covid and I want to draw the line. And whether it is the cost of business or the cost of living, the only way we deal with these in the long term is growth.

headlines.title: Alleged killers of Australian surfers and American friend go on trial in Mexico
headlines.description: Three men on trial for killing Jake and Callum Robinson and Jack Carter Rhoad in Baja California in 2024 The alleged killers of two Australian surfers and an American at a Mexican surfing hotspot in 2024 have gone on trial in the border resort where the three were murdered. The Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, respectively, and their 30-year-old American friend Jack Carter Rhoad were shot dead after being robbed in Mexico’s violence-hit Baja California .

headlines.title: Polanski faces Green rival in his pursuit of Keir Starmer’s old seat
headlines.description: Hamza Chowdhury says most of his fellow Green Camden councillors back him to contest 8 October byelection UK politics live – latest updates Zack Polanski is facing unexpected opposition from his own party in his attempt to fight the Holborn and St Pancras byelection for the Greens, with a local councillor saying he is also seeking the nomination, and that the seat does not need “a politician you’ll only see on a leaflet”. The intervention by Hamza Chowdhury, a Green representative on Camden council in north London, came as the date for the byelection was confirmed for 8 October, after Keir Starmer’s formal resignation as an MP.

headlines.title: Syrian reactor could have been used for nuclear weapons if completed, UN says
headlines.description: Chief of nuclear watchdog says secret Assad-era facility would have been able to produce fissile material A nearly complete nuclear reactor built secretly during the rule of the toppled Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad would have been able to produce fissile material for possible use in nuclear weapons, the chief of the UN nuclear watchdog has revealed. Inspectors from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) last month visited two sites, one in Deir ez-Zor and a second in an undisclosed location identified to them by Syrian authorities.

headlinePool.title: Europe’s centre fears nationalist wave after AfD victory but only has itself to blame
headlinePool.description: Saxony-Anhalt win part of wider trend driven by mainstream policy failures and gradual normalisation of far right ideas Europe live – latest updates The numbers speak for themselves: Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), a party that dabbles in Nazi imagery, distinguishes between “biological” and “passport” Germans, and is too extreme even for France’s far-right leader Marine Le Pen, nearly doubled its score in Sunday’s state election in Saxony-Anhalt to 43.8% of the vote. Meanwhile, the centre-right CDU of the chancellor, Friedrich Merz, collapsed to 17.2%, less than half its total in the same race five years ago, and the centre-left SPD – Germany’s other main party of government for the past 60-odd years – scraped 9.3%. The least that can be said is that the centre did not hold.

headlinePool.title: Indonesia volcano eruption leaves 340,000 stranded as airports extend closure
headlinePool.description: Anak Krakatau, which lies about 150km from capital Jakarta, began spewing lava and volvanic ash late on Friday.

headlinePool.title: No 10 condemns ‘thuggish’ far-right activists after Portsmouth unrest
headlinePool.description: Hundreds of men, some in balaclavas, try to prevent asylum seekers’ processing, two days after similar scenes in Dover UK politics live – latest updates Downing Street has condemned the “thuggish and intimidating behaviour” of far-right activists who blocked roads in Portsmouth when a boat carrying asylum seekers arrived in the city, two days after similar scenes in Dover. Hundreds of men, some dressed in black and wearing balaclavas, tried to stop the arrivals from being transported for processing until 3am, when police removed them with threats of arrest.

headlinePool.title: Merz says ‘shock’ AfD victory in key German state ‘is an election result we cannot simply move past’ – as it happened
headlinePool.description: German chancellor says vote for far-right party ‘will have repercussions’ across the country Far-right AfD wins key German state election but falls just short of majority AfD’s Chrupalla continues in this vein, saying the German public wants to see a change in direction, and specifically saying the electorate is “fed up” as the government keeps “transferring billions of our tax money to Ukraine … instead of using it for our own population.” He says the party has “a clear mandate” to rule in Saxony-Anhalt and will hold discussions with others about what can be done.

headlinePool.title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status
headlinePool.description: The long-running claim alleges Grindr breached UK privacy laws by sharing data with third parties.

headlinePool.title: French winemakers forecast 30-year low harvest after severe drought and heat
headlinePool.description: Estimates suggest drop in production with vineyards also concerned ‘smoke taint’ from wildfires may affect quality French vineyards hit by severe drought and heatwaves are expected to report a 30-year low in wine production after the country’s hottest ever recorded summer, according to the agriculture ministry. Initial estimates suggest winemakers will produce just under 34m hectolitres from this year’s harvest: a drop of 6% on last year, and 17% less than ‌the 2021-2025 average.

headlinePool.title: Stolen Generations survivors have more health challenges than other First Nations people
headlinePool.description: Indigenous Australians forcibly removed under government policies more likely to have severe or profound disability, report finds The report by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW) was commissioned by peak advocacy body the Healing Foundation, which supports Stolen Generations survivors and their families, and builds on existing data released in 2023.

headlinePool.title: Record strength El Niño could mean bigger supermarket bills for Australians, experts warn
headlinePool.description: Predicted hot and dry weather in growing areas in eastern Australia identified as ‘one of the key issues’ that will affect food prices over next 12 months The Bureau of Meteorology has forecast El Niño will peak in late spring or summer and “reach levels above the warmest observed since reliable records began in 1950”.

headlinePool.title: Grassroots Labor group urges Albanese government to chart course away from ‘American war machine’
headlinePool.description: Pressure follows revelations US military and weapons manufacturers control or have access to more than 100 bases across Australian continent Why can the US access so many Australian military bases? – podcast The Australian government has defended the growing presence of the US military on the Australian continent, insisting the defence sites “are Australian bases under Australian control”, despite evidence the US military controls more than a dozen bases on Australian territory.
